definition: Cost Per Click. The amount you pay each time someone clicks on your ad. In B2B legal tech, LinkedIn CPCs typically range from $5-15 CAD, while Google Search CPCs range from $3-8 CAD.
Cost Per Mille (thousand impressions). The cost to show your ad 1,000 times. CPM-based buying is common for awareness campaigns where the goal is visibility rather than clicks.

Click-Through Rate. The percentage of people who click your ad after seeing it. Calculated as clicks divided by impressions. A 0.4% CTR on LinkedIn is actually good for B2B legal tech — the industry average is around 0.3%.
Cost Per Acquisition (or Cost Per Action). The average cost to get one conversion — such as a demo request, form fill, or sign-up. CPA = Total Spend / Number of Conversions.
Return On Ad Spend. Revenue generated for every dollar spent on advertising. A ROAS of 4:1 means $4 revenue for every $1 spent. Different from ROI because it only considers ad spend, not total costs.
Return On Investment. Net profit relative to total investment including ad spend, labor, tools, and overhead. Calculated as (Revenue - Total Costs) / Total Costs × 100. More comprehensive than ROAS.
A single instance of your ad being displayed on someone's screen. One impression is counted each time an ad is shown, regardless of whether the user interacts with it.
When someone taps or clicks on your ad, typically directing them to a landing page. Clicks are the basis for CPC pricing and CTR calculations.
A completed desired action — form submission, demo request, download, sign-up, or purchase. Tracked via pixels or conversion tags. The ultimate measure of campaign effectiveness.
A potential customer who has provided contact information or taken a qualifying action. In B2B legal tech, leads typically come from form fills, content downloads, or demo requests.

Marketing Qualified Lead. A lead deemed more likely to become a customer based on engagement criteria — content downloads, email opens, website visits, or lead scoring in HubSpot. MQLs are passed to sales for further qualification.

Sales Qualified Lead. A lead vetted by the sales team and confirmed as a genuine potential customer. SQLs have shown clear intent — requesting demos, asking for pricing, or engaging directly with sales.

Showing ads to people who have already visited your website or engaged with your content but didn't convert. Uses tracking pixels to follow visitors across the web. Usually the highest-ROI tactic available.

A targeting method where platforms find new users who share characteristics with your existing customers. Upload a customer list, and the platform finds similar people. Great for expanding reach to qualified prospects.

Running two or more variations of an ad simultaneously to see which performs better. Only change one variable at a time (headline, image, CTA) to isolate what works. Essential for improving performance over time.

A standalone web page designed for a specific campaign. Users 'land' here after clicking an ad. Effective landing pages match the ad's message, have one clear call-to-action, and remove distracting navigation.

Tags appended to URLs that tell analytics tools where traffic came from. The five standard UTMs: utm_source (platform), utm_medium (channel type), utm_campaign (campaign name), utm_term (keyword), utm_content (ad variant). Essential for tracking which ads drive results.

A snippet of JavaScript code placed on your website that tracks user behavior and conversions. When someone visits a page with the pixel, it sends data back to the ad platform. Required for retargeting and conversion tracking.

The initial 2-4 weeks after launching a campaign when the ad platform's algorithm is gathering data and optimizing delivery. Performance will be volatile — don't panic or make major changes. Platforms typically need 25-50 conversions to exit learning phase. This is the #1 thing beginners don't understand.

Google Ads metric (1-10) estimating the quality of your keywords, ads, and landing pages. Based on expected CTR, ad relevance, and landing page experience. Higher Quality Scores = lower CPCs and better ad positions. Worth optimizing.

Rating used by Meta and LinkedIn measuring how well your ad resonates with your audience. Based on positive signals (clicks, conversions) and negative signals (ad hides). Higher relevance = lower costs and better delivery.

Third-party websites and apps where ad platforms can show your ads beyond their own platform. Google Display Network and Meta Audience Network are examples. Extends reach but may perform differently than native placements.

Audience segments built from your own data — customer email lists, website visitors, app users. Upload your data to ad platforms, which match it to user profiles. More precise than interest-based targeting.

The time period after someone clicks or views your ad during which a conversion is credited to that ad. Common windows: 1-day click, 7-day click, 28-day click. B2B typically needs longer windows due to longer sales cycles.

When someone sees your ad (but doesn't click it) and later converts. Helps measure the impact of display and video ads that influence decisions without generating clicks. Controversial but valuable for understanding full impact.

How your advertising account is organized: Campaign → Ad Group (or Ad Set) → Individual Ads. Good structure aligns with business goals, enables budget control, and makes optimization easier. Usually organized by product, funnel stage, or audience.

Methods for setting how much you'll pay for ad placements. Manual CPC (you set bids), Target CPA (platform optimizes for conversions), Maximize Clicks (platform gets most clicks for budget). Start with manual, move to automated once you have conversion data.

Determines your ad's position on search results and whether it shows at all. In Google Ads: Bid Amount × Quality Score × Expected Impact of Extensions. You can outrank competitors who bid more by having better quality and relevance.

Keywords that prevent your ad from showing for irrelevant searches. If selling premium legal software, add 'free,' 'cheap,' 'jobs' as negatives to avoid wasted spend. Review your search terms report regularly to find new negatives.

Scheduling ads to run only during specific hours or days. For B2B legal tech, you might run ads only during business hours (9-6 Mon-Fri) when lawyers are at work. Saves budget and can improve conversion rates.

Delivering ads based on geographic location — country, province/state, city, or radius. Essential for Dye & Durham given operations in Canada, UK, and Australia. Each geography has different platform costs and regulations.

ROAS measures revenue vs. ad spend only. ROI measures profit vs. ALL costs (ad spend + labor + tools + overhead). A campaign can have great ROAS (5:1) but negative ROI if operational costs are high. Always know which you're measuring.

Sending conversion data from your server directly to ad platforms, bypassing the user's browser. More reliable than pixels because it's not blocked by ad blockers or browser privacy settings. Increasingly important as browsers restrict cookies.

Data you collect directly from your audience — website behavior, CRM data, email engagement, purchase history. The most valuable and privacy-compliant data source. Use HubSpot contact lists for Custom Audiences on ad platforms.

Data collected by entities without a direct user relationship, aggregated and sold to advertisers. Includes demographic and behavioral segments. Declining in value due to privacy regulations (GDPR, CASL) and cookie deprecation.

Percentage of available impressions your ads received vs. what they could have received. Lost impression share comes from budget limits or low ad rank. Aim for 80%+ on brand terms, 50-70% on competitive terms.

Percentage of search impressions your ads received specifically on search results pages. Key competitive metric — if you're at 40%, competitors are capturing 60% of available searches. Increase with higher bids or better Quality Score.

Rules for crediting conversions to different touchpoints. Last-click (common default) gives all credit to the final click. First-click credits the initial touchpoint. Linear splits evenly. Data-driven (best) uses machine learning. Model choice significantly impacts budget decisions.

The stages a prospect moves through: Awareness (top) → Consideration (middle) → Conversion (bottom). Different channels, messaging, and metrics apply at each stage. LinkedIn works great for awareness; Google Search captures conversion-ready prospects.

Campaign objective focused on visibility and recognition. Prioritizes reach and impressions over direct conversions. Measured by ad recall lift, reach, and frequency. Important for new market entries — you can't sell to people who don't know you exist.

Campaign objective focused on capturing contact information. Uses forms, gated content, demos, and webinars. Measured by cost per lead, lead quality, and MQL conversion rate. The primary campaign type for B2B legal tech marketing.

Visual banner ads shown on websites across ad networks. Common sizes: 300x250, 728x90, 160x600 pixels. Great for awareness and retargeting but lower intent than search ads. Google Display Network reaches 90%+ of internet users.

Text ads on search engine results pages, triggered by keyword searches. High intent — people are actively looking for solutions. Google Ads is the dominant platform. Requires keyword research and ongoing optimization.

Ads on social media platforms — LinkedIn, Meta (Facebook/Instagram), etc. LinkedIn offers the best B2B targeting (job title, company, industry). Meta is cheaper but less precise for B2B. Both support multiple ad formats.

Automated buying and selling of ad inventory using software and algorithms in real-time. Includes real-time bidding (RTB) and private marketplace deals. Advanced — not recommended until you've mastered Google Ads and LinkedIn.

Demand-Side Platform. Technology for buying ad inventory across multiple exchanges through one interface. Examples: Google DV360, The Trade Desk, StackAdapt. Typically requires higher budgets ($3K+/month) and more expertise.
Digital marketplace connecting advertisers (via DSPs) with publishers (via SSPs) for real-time ad trading. Think of it as a stock exchange for ad impressions. Google Ad Exchange is the largest.
Average number of times one person sees your ad. Too low (1-2) means insufficient impact. Too high (10+) causes ad fatigue. Sweet spot for B2B is typically 3-7 times over a campaign's duration.
Total number of unique people who see your ad at least once. Unlike impressions (which count repeat views), reach measures audience breadth. Critical metric for awareness campaigns.

Percentage of people who interact with your ad (likes, comments, shares, clicks, video views). Calculated as engagements ÷ impressions × 100. Higher engagement signals content resonance and usually leads to lower costs.

Percentage of visitors who land on a page and leave without any further action. High bounce rate = mismatch between ad promise and landing page delivery, poor UX, or slow load time. Aim for under 40% on campaign landing pages.

Average cost to generate one lead. Total ad spend ÷ number of leads. In B2B legal tech, expect $50-200 CAD per lead on LinkedIn, $20-80 on Google Search. Varies significantly by audience, offer, and geography.

Total cost to acquire one new paying customer — including ALL marketing and sales expenses, not just ad spend. Compare against Lifetime Value (LTV) for sustainability. A healthy LTV:CAC ratio is 3:1 or higher.

Predicted total revenue from a customer over their entire relationship with your company. Consider repeat purchases, upsells, retention rate. In legal tech SaaS, LTV can be substantial due to long contracts and expansion revenue.
